data.exact_reserve_text:
The underwriting profit includes releases from reserves established in prior years of GBP 38.3 million (2014: GBP 8.2 million).
The claims ratio significantly improved to 33% (2014: 51%) as a result of a benign year in terms of catastrophe activity, a lower volume of larger losses and increased prior period reserve releases predominantly driven by releases on Catastrophe North America and Special Risk classes.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Large catastrophe losses in 2014 that contributed to higher claims in that year.

prior_year_events.event_name: Commutation of Special Purpose Syndicate 6106 balances / settlements
prior_year_events.impact_description: Commutation and settlement activity relating to prior underwriting years (2012/2013), with amounts retained/settled between Syndicate 2001 and Syndicate 6106 affecting inter-syndicate balances and runoff.

named_events.loss_description: The largest loss event for the year impacting the SBU was the winter freeze in January and February 2015 amounting to GBP 11.4 million.
The Tianjin explosion in August 2015 amounting to GBP 7.7 million.
Large catastrophe losses of GBP 26.6 million (Nebraska PCS 45 and 48) in 2014.
Property and Casualty was impacted by a number of losses including GBP 6 million on UK Floods.

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2015 Syndicate 2001 carried gross claims outstanding of GBP 1,657.7m. During 2015 there was a net prior year release on claims of GBP 53.5m (a c.3.2% reduction versus opening gross reserves). Management attribute the release primarily to favourable prior period claims development driven by a benign catastrophe year (fewer large catastrophes), lower frequency of large commercial motor losses, and specific reserve releases in Catastrophe North America and Special Risk classes. The release supported an improved combined ratio and contributed to the underwriting profit, with notable named losses in 2015 (winter freeze and Tianjin explosion) being modest versus reserves.
raw_causal_phrases: releases from reserves established in prior years of GBP 38.3 million (2014: GBP 8.2 million).
increased prior period reserve releases predominantly driven by releases on Catastrophe North America and Special Risk classes.
absence of a large catastrophe loss experience during the year
a lower volume of larger losses
data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding and the gross prior year movement are taken directly from the Insurance liabilities column of the claims movement table (note 9(a)) and are high confidence. Narrative references (e.g. 'releases of GBP 38.3m') are net of reinsurance and thus differ from the gross movement; the gross movement (-GBP 53.5m) per the movement table was used as authoritative. Divisional gross premium totals were used for premium mix (these do not exactly sum to the total in some tables due to minor other items). Claims development triangle is present but contains an aggregate '2010 and prior' column (excluded from the UW year list). There was commutation activity (Syndicate 6106) during the period which can distort inter-syndicate balances and runoff.
